# Grid Traversal and Data Structures


## Overview
This family encompasses methods that adapt the domain traversal and data structures of [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) to handle sparse, hierarchical, or multi-resolution volumetric data, avoiding the memory and computational costs of dense regular grids [G]. Unlike standard grid-based methods that iterate over fixed arrays, these techniques traverse octrees, sparse point sets, or [adaptive mesh refinement](#5344-adaptive-mesh-refinement-amr-data-structures.md) (AMR) boundaries, dynamically [gathering](#9569-gathering.md) scalar values and generating geometry only where necessary [G]. They are distinguished from their siblings by their specific approach to handling topological discontinuities, such as cracks at level boundaries, through mechanisms like uniform node sizing, dynamic lookup, or explicit [stitch cell generation](#10250-3d-amr-grid-stitching.md) [G].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Octree-based Isosurfacing](1247-octree-based-isosurfacing.md)
Replaces the uniform [Cartesian grid](#3-dense-grids-and-memory-layout.md) with an [octree](#18524-octree.md) spatial subdivision to enable adaptive resolution. It sets itself apart by decoupling spatial resolution from global grid density, though it sacrifices the topological guarantees of [uniform grids](#3950-regular-grid.md), potentially introducing cracks if the octree is not sufficiently adapted to the surface geometry. Choose this when the scalar field is sparse or has varying feature scales.

### [Grid Traversal and Data Structure Adaptation](8340-grid-traversal-and-data-structure-adaptation.md)
A broad category for adapting traversal to sparse, hierarchical, or AMR data. It distinguishes itself through specific crack-prevention strategies employed by its children, such as uniform node sizing or dynamic lookup. Choose this as the conceptual framework for implementing custom adaptive extractors.

### [Crack-free Isosurface Extraction from AMR Data](9981-crack-free-isosurface-extraction-from-amr-data.md)
Extracts watertight [isosurfaces](#13788-isosurfaces.md) from block-structured AMR data in distributed-memory parallel environments. It solves the problem of T-junctions (cracks) arising from standard Marching Cubes on hierarchical data by using ghost cells and a dual-grid representation. Choose this when processing data from codes like BoxLib or Chombo where memory efficiency and parallel scalability are critical.

## Background
The development of adaptive [grid traversal](#14347-grid-traversal-one-pass-over-allocated.md) methods addresses the limitations of uniform grids in representing complex, sparse, or multi-scale phenomena efficiently [G]. Standard isosurface extraction methods assume a regular topology, leading to excessive memory usage when applied to large volumes with localized features [G]. Octree-based and AMR-aware extraction methods represent fine details near the isosurface while coarsening empty regions [G]. This family is essential in scientific visualization for data generated by adaptive mesh refinement codes such as BoxLib, Chombo, SAM-RAI, and Enzo [Crack-free Isosurface Extraction from AMR Data](9981-crack-free-isosurface-extraction-from-amr-data.md).
